source: Young & Freedman, University Physics with Modern Physics, 15th edition

items.finding: Recovered theory omitted the0.01Pa vacuum condition, the assumption ignoring differences of electrode materials, and the tanning/melanin application.
items.resolution: All three restored after direct page comparison. Removed an unsupported numerical1ns latency bound and the unsupported identification of the measured cathode as a specific oxide.

items.finding: Recovered text described28 photons and a fourth million-photon panel.
items.resolution: Image and text now agree on exactly three panels:21,1000,10000 photons.

items.finding: Slit-width estimates and momentum-spread estimates are not automatically standard deviations.
items.resolution: The rough slit derivation is separated from the standard-deviation inequality. Approximation signs are retained in small-angle/rough-width steps. No false derivation of the exact hbar/2 constant from an aperture width.

items.finding: The source gives85 percent as the fraction in the central maximum. Integration of the ideal one-dimensional Fraunhofer sinc-squared distribution gives0.90282333358.
items.resolution: Both the rough85-percent description and the more precise90-percent ideal-model result are explained. Neither fraction enters the uncertainty derivation.

items.finding: Recovered text called3lambda/(2a) the exact first secondary maximum.
items.resolution: It is the nonzero-intensity choice among the stated approximate diffraction minima. The unsupported exact-maximum claim is removed.

items.finding: A relative spectral width is not a sharp interval within which all photon frequencies are guaranteed to lie.
items.resolution: The5.3-percent width is described under the example's pulse convention, not as a hard spectral cutoff. Photon count is an estimated mean.

items.finding: Text extraction misreads the final microjoule label as millijoule.
items.resolution: The actual page image and calculation agree on1.91microjoule. This is an OCR issue, not a printed-unit error.

items.finding: The proposed0.100nm to0.110nm change exceeds the maximum free-electron Compton shift.
items.resolution: An energy-difference candidate is distinguished from the impossibility of the stated single free-electron scattering event.

items.finding: The uncertainty lower bound is not the first-minimum diffraction width.
items.resolution: Both quantities are calculated and distinguished, including the caution about treating a hard slit width as a position standard deviation.

items.finding: OCR misreads450microseconds and2.0micrograms as milliseconds and milligrams.
items.resolution: Page image read directly. Calculation uses450e-6seconds and2.0e-9kilograms.

items.finding: Literal switch labels in FigureP38.38 place a on the accelerating polarity and b on the retarding polarity, opposite to the intended sequence.
items.resolution: Figure unchanged. Literal polarity is identified first. Quantitative answers are conditional on using the intended retarding/accelerating branches, equivalent to swapping switch names in the text. Kirchhoff residual checked.

items.finding: Pair creation needs target recoil, including target rest energy and momentum conservation.
items.resolution: Exact recoil derived before low-speed expansion. No finite-energy stationary-target solution asserted.

items.finding: The CO2 laser wavelength is10.6micrometers, not millimeters.
items.resolution: Direct image reading, exact inverse-Compton expression and final electron momentum sign checked.

items.finding: Fixed power, fixed photon flux, emission latency and statistical waiting time are different constraints.
items.resolution: Each constraint is explicit. No blanket claim that increasing frequency leaves saturation current unchanged under every condition.
